standard.confidence_text: approximately the 95 % level, usually k = 2 (A2LA scope, footnote 2)
standard.reference: Calibration Scope of Accreditation, A2LA 1888.03, rev. 07/07/2026, section V, printed p. 9 of 47 (DC Current - Generate, Transconductance amplifier/coil) and p. 30 of 47 (AC Current - Generate (cont), Clamp-On Only, Multifunction calibrator/coil); Fluke 5500A/COIL technical data (10/2026)
standard.author: written by specs/build_coil_standard.py from the scope pages

notes.1: SOURCE: the laboratory's own A2LA scope of accreditation, certificate 1888.03 (revised 07/07/2026), section V. Electrical - DC/Low Frequency. DC rows: printed p. 9 of 47, "DC Current - Generate" (last block): (2 to 20) A 90 uA/A + 0.1 mA; (20 to 120) A 80 uA/A + 8 mA; (120 to 3000) A 0.8 % + 0.08 A; comment "Transconductance amplifier/coil". AC rows: printed p. 30 of 47, "AC Current - Generate (cont)", "Clamp-On Only", (20.5 to 1025) A: (45 to 65) Hz 0.8 %; (65 to 440) Hz 0.99 %; comment "Multifunction calibrator/coil". Built by specs/build_coil_standard.py.
notes.2: VERIFICATION: the five lines above (and the column headers: CMC 2, 5, 9 (+/-); no frequency column on p. 9, a Frequency column on p. 30) were read from the RENDERED PAGE IMAGES of pp. 9 and 30 of 47, each read twice (full page, then a 200 dpi crop), on 2026-10-23. Both pages carry "(A2LA Cert. No. 1888.03) Revised 07/07/2026". The coil datasheet values in note 7 were also read from the rendered pages. The extracted text was used only to find the pages.
notes.3: CONFIDENCE: footnote 2 of the scope: a CMC is an EXPANDED uncertainty at approximately the 95 % level of confidence, usually using a coverage factor of k = 2. Stored as confidence_pct 95, so the coverage divisor is 2.0 (u of the standard = CMC / 2). Wording kept in confidence_text.
notes.4: TERMS: footnote 5: the first percentage is a percentage of the READING unless otherwise noted; footnote 9: a CMC is a percent or fraction of the reading plus a fixed floor. Stored in the repo's usual form: rel (fraction of the reading) and abs (fixed term, amperes), computed in Decimal: 90 uA/A = 90 ppm = 9e-05 and 80 uA/A = 8e-05 of reading, 0.8 % = 0.008, 0.99 % = 0.0099; 0.1 mA = 1e-04 A, 8 mA = 0.008 A, 0.08 A. The two AC rows have no fixed term (the scope prints a bare percentage). A CMC has no 90 day / 1 yr column: each row is stored once, under the period "1 yr" (the default period of every standard).
notes.5: DC ROWS (p. 9 of 47): scope parameter "DC Current - Generate", comment "Transconductance amplifier/coil", column header "Parameter/Equipment | Range | CMC (+/-) | Comments" - there is NO frequency column, these are DC ranges (rows kind DCI). Stored with direction "output" (the lab generates the current) and no frequency. The comment says "Transconductance amplifier/coil", NOT "Multifunction calibrator/coil": see note 9 (OWNER QUESTION).
notes.6: AC ROWS (p. 30 of 47): scope parameter "AC Current - Generate (cont)", sub-heading "Clamp-On Only", range (20.5 to 1025) A, Frequency column (45 to 65) Hz 0.8 % and (65 to 440) Hz 0.99 % (percent of reading only), comment "Multifunction calibrator/coil". "Clamp-On Only" is kept as a qualifier of the row (the bracket of the function name, the repo's variant field). A frequency inside a band is required for a lookup; at 65 Hz both bands match and the larger limit is used (the scope CMC rule).
notes.7: COIL DATASHEET (Fluke 5500A/COIL | 50-Turn Current Coil, technical data 10/2026, read from the rendered pages; facts only, none is used in a calculation): number of turns 50; maximum current 11 A rms continuous, 20 A rms for 2 minutes; duty-cycle derating: below 11 A continuous, above 11 A 2 minutes ON / 8 minutes OFF; maximum voltage 3 V rms; frequency of operation DC, 45-440 Hz (should not exceed the rms voltage rating): for the 5500A current output DC and 45-65 Hz 0-11 A, 65-440 Hz 0-2.19999 A; for the 5520A current output DC and 45-65 Hz 0-20 A, 65-440 Hz 0-2.99999 A (assumes a Fluke 80i-600 clamp or equivalent; other clamps may limit the drive to less); minimum inside diameter of the clamp jaws 2.54 cm (1 in.); statement of calibration practices included, with a 17025 accredited report. The coil multiplies the calibrator current by 50 (effective output = 50 x calibrator current).
notes.8: COIL / CLAMP INTERACTION UNCERTAINTY (datasheet, NOT added to the scope rows): +/-(0.25 % of effective output + 0.5 A) for toroidal-wound current clamps such as the Fluke 80I and 80I-1000; +/-(0.50 % of effective output + 0.5 A) for clamps like the Fluke 80i-kw, 80i-400, 80i-410, 80i-500, 80i-1010, Fluke 31, Fluke 33 or equivalent. It is a contribution of the clamp meter / coil pair, which the scope CMC excludes; the repo has no second-term mechanism for a standard, so it is recorded here only and combined with nothing (no combination rule is invented; whether and how it enters the uncertainty is an OWNER DECISION).
notes.9: EFFECTIVE CURRENT AND WHICH LINES BELONG TO THE COIL: the scope ranges are the current the clamp sees ("effective output" in the datasheet). The Clamp-On Only upper limit 1025 A = 20.5 A x 50 turns (an inference: the maximum current of the scope's multifunction-calibrator ranges times the coil's turns, not stated by the scope). Observations for the owner: (a) the datasheet limits the 65-440 Hz current to 2.19999 A (5500A) or 2.99999 A (5520A), i.e. 110 A or 150 A effective, while the 65-440 Hz row is listed to 1025 A; (b) the DC rows run to 3000 A, beyond 50 x 20 A = 1000 A, and their comment is "Transconductance amplifier/coil". Both are stored as printed on the scope.
notes.10: NOT STORED: the scope's other coil-related lines (AC Current - Generate (20.5 to 3000) A, (16 to 850) Hz 0.7 % + 0.84 A and (0.85 to 6) kHz 0.8 % + 0.84 A, "Transconductance amplifier/coil"; DC Power - Generate, "Multifunction calibrator with current coil") because they were not asked for; and the clamp meter's own contribution (resolution, repeatability, positioning in the jaws). The CMC excludes the unit under test; a certificate value may be larger.
notes.11: USE: the lookups find this sheet by its model id (uncertainty_budget.build(kind, ..., standard="A2LA-5500A-COIL"), tartur.standard_accuracy, tartur.compute(..., standard=...)). It is NOT offered in any calibrator picker: those choose the instrument that is commanded, and the coil is not commanded. The Fluke 365 procedure uses a 20-turn coil and keeps the regular calibrator current uncertainty, unscaled (owner decision); nothing here changes it.

limits.limit: 50 turns; 11 A rms continuous, 20 A rms 2 min; interaction +/-(0.25 % or 0.50 % of effective output + 0.5 A), not added; jaws >= 2.54 cm.

problems.what: This is the laboratory's own CMC (expanded, approximately 95 %, usually k = 2), not a manufacturer specification. No 90 day / 1 yr columns; stored under the period "1 yr".
Comment on the scope is "Transconductance amplifier/coil", not "Multifunction calibrator/coil"; the three DC rows run to 3000 A, beyond 50 turns x 20 A. Stored as printed (note 9).

problems.where: Current, AC [Clamp-On Only, Multifunction calibrator/coil] / (65 to 440) Hz
problems.what: The datasheet limits 65-440 Hz drive to 2.19999 A (5500A) / 2.99999 A (5520A), about 110 / 150 A effective, below the 1025 A of the scope row (note 9). Stored as printed.
The datasheet's clamp/coil interaction uncertainty (0.25 % or 0.50 % of effective output + 0.5 A) is NOT added to these rows: no second-term mechanism exists for a standard (note 8).
